comments.content: Re-enqueue updates the payload of a `failed` row but never resets its `state` back to `'pending'` (nor clears `error`/`attempts`). Since `claim()` only selects `state='pending'`, a row that ever reaches `'failed'` can never be claimed again — the item is silently dropped from every later run, so the job never converges and reports fewer processed files than exist. This is the opposite of the resume guarantee the file advertises. Reset the state (and clear `error`) when adopting a new payload.

comments.content: `jobDir()` maps disallowed characters to `_` and truncates to 64 chars, so distinct ids can collide onto one directory (`"a/b"` vs `"a_b"`, or ids differing only past 64 chars), letting unrelated jobs share a `queue.sqlite`. Also, `.` is allowed by the character class and only `..` sequences are collapsed, so an id of `"."` (or `""`) resolves to the jobs root itself and writes the queue/results into the shared parent directory. Consider hashing the id or rejecting unsafe ids.
